post.caption: Cartier's gems waited decades for a name. In the 1920s, Cartier began combining carved gems from India into bright jewels. Jacques Cartier first visited India in 1911, for the Delhi Durbar, and brought home carved emeralds and rubies, many shaped like leaves and berries. Cartier chose bold color over perfect clarity. At the time nobody called the style Tutti Frutti. That name only came into use in the 1970s, and it is Italian for all fruits. Cartier protected the name in 1989. One 1928 Cartier bandeau splits into two bracelets.
